name: Malik Nabers

background.fact: Born July 28, 2003 in Lafayette, Louisiana; he played his senior year at Southside High School in Youngsville, Louisiana, but could not play football that year because his transfer waiver was denied. In his last high school season he led Louisiana with 58 catches, 1,223 yards and 21 touchdowns.

At LSU he was a unanimous All-American in 2023, led the FBS with 1,569 receiving yards that year, and finished as LSU's all-time leader in receiving yards with 3,003. He was MVP of the 2023 Citrus Bowl.
The Giants drafted him sixth overall in 2024 (round 1, pick 6); he set several rookie receiver and franchise records.

recent_events.fact: On the last drive the Giants threw deep on consecutive plays, first to Darnell Mooney and then to Nabers, and J.J. McCarthy's final pass was intercepted by Rasul Douglas. Nabers said afterward that getting the ball out quickly against the blitz was the better play, and he took responsibility for his own fumble. Many fans read this as blaming McCarthy; reports say he did not blame him directly.
